comments.body:
Review remediation (2026-08-21) — narration moved out of the description to keep it under the
plan-review admission limit. Record of what was factually wrong in the original plan and what was
corrected, with file:line evidence.

1. Vacuous guard. The original acceptance criterion was `grep -rn '"-m", "pytest"' tests/`. That
   returns ZERO hits on unmodified `main`, because Black splits every argv list one element per
   line, so the two literals never appear adjacent in source. The criterion therefore passed
   vacuously both before and after the work. The guard is now an AST scan over `tests/**/*.py` for
   `subprocess.run`/`Popen` calls whose first argument is a list literal containing `sys.executable`,
   `"-m"` and `"pytest"` in sequence, plus a definition-count check
   (`grep -rn '^def run_nested_pytest' tests/` == 1).

2. Wrong site count. Fourteen `sys.executable -m pytest` launch sites exist under `tests/`, not
   fifteen. The plan's "twelve other sites found by `grep -rln`" resolved to zero files, for the
   same Black-formatting reason as (1).

3. Bug status. All three cited `--basetemp` bugs are CLOSED: `bf7c-333e-29b0-4ee4`
   (grindable-deviant-angwantibo, repaired `tests/_store_isolation.py:33-50`),
   `444d-62ff-2c3c-42a9` (acidic-ferreous-mole, repaired the parity collection child now at
   `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:839-856`), and `fb03-2609-ef83-4b41`
   (asbestos-popular-tench, which inventoried every launch site and repaired the executing children
   in `tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py` and `tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py`). Session
   log `0bd6-4729-e79e-433b` (kilted-centauric-cardinal) root-caused the shutdown timeout to pytest
   session-finish `cleanup_numbered_dir` owning liveness.

4. Two of the three files the plan described as "missing `--basetemp`" already have it:
   `tests/_store_isolation.py:41` and `tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:848`.

5. The sites genuinely lacking `--basetemp` today are
   `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py:25`,
   `tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py:165` and
   `tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:162`. The first EXECUTES three real integration
   nodes and is a live instance of the same defect; it was absent from both the asbestos inventory
   (it is `pytest.mark.integration`) and the original Scope. The other two are `--collect-only`
   children, which asbestos classified non-applicable because a collect-only child never allocates
   `TempPathFactory._basetemp`.

6. Two sites must NOT be converted. `tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py:154` (bug 291e)
   and `tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:92` (bug a371) launch the BARE `pytest` console
   script from a cwd outside the repository on purpose, so the repo root cannot reach `sys.path`.
   Routing them through `sys.executable -m pytest` inserts cwd and voids both reproductions.

7. Verbatim `env` is a security requirement, not a convenience. Four sites
   (`tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_env_repr_security.py:31`,
   `tests/unit/test_environ_assert_repr_security.py:134`,
   `tests/unit/test_fixture_env_repr_security.py:49`,
   `tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py:189`) pass a deliberately minimal two- or
   three-key mapping so pytest's bounded mapping repr cannot truncate the sentinel away. If the
   helper merges onto `os.environ` or otherwise widens the mapping, all four oracles go
   green-but-vacuous.

8. The call contract is pinned by `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_deadline_heldout.py`: `timeout`
   must reach `subprocess.run` as a KEYWORD and stay `>= 30` (`:42`); the `CompletedProcess` must be
   returned by identity (`:51`, `result is nested_result`); and a plain-`dict` env
   (`{"PATH": "test-path"}`, `:39`) must survive without any `SubprocessEnv` method being called on
   it. `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` must also propagate so
   `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:105-108` keeps converting it into its own diagnostic.

9. Prose false positives. The unquoted string `-m pytest` occurs 23 times across 16 files as prose,
   regex and docstring data (`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:640,651,652`,
   `tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py:89`, `tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:8-13`,
   `tests/module_size_support.py:17`, and ten `tests/scripts/**` module docstrings). The guard
   deliberately does not match it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Review remediation round 2 (2026-08-21). Three further factual defects found by re-running every claim against the tree at origin/main; all now corrected in the description.

A. The guard's AST shape was wrong. The previous description specified a scan for subprocess.run/Popen calls 'whose FIRST ARGUMENT is a list literal'. Running exactly that shape returns 13 sites, not 14: tests/unit/test_fixture_env_repr_security.py builds the argv into a local 'command' variable at :54 and passes it at :67, so a call-argument-only scan never sees it. The guard is now specified as a scan over ANY list-or-tuple literal in tests/**/*.py holding sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest' in consecutive positions; that shape returns exactly the 14 sites in Scope.

B. Blocking finding G6 (env on the parity collector) is real and confirmed. tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:839 (_collect_node_ids) passes NO env to subprocess.run and therefore inherits os.environ today. tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity_basetemp.py:32 sets PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT with monkeypatch.setenv on the parent and asserts at :37-40 that the child honoured it, so that oracle depends on the inheritance. Under the REQUIRED-verbatim-env rule the converted site must pass env=subprocess_env() (tests/_subprocess_env.py:37 copies os.environ into the repr-safe mapping). A second site has the same shape: tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:62 passes neither env nor cwd. Both are now named explicitly.

C. Advisory G1G2 (tmp_path on the parity collector) is real. _collect_node_ids(paths, selection) takes no tmp_path fixture and sources its basetemp from tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='rebar-pytest-collect-'); its two-argument signature is pinned by name at test_ci_workflow_parity_basetemp.py:9,33. The description now states that it keeps that TemporaryDirectory and hands Path(temp_dir) to the helper as tmp_path, and passes no_cacheprovider=False to match the flag it omits today.

D. AC arithmetic corrected. The previous AC claimed 'grep -rln -- --basetemp tests/ returning only tests/_nested_pytest.py'. Run today that grep returns twelve modules, and after the conversion it returns TWO, because tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py:169 spells --basetemp and is deliberately not converted (bug 291e). The AC now asserts a count of 2 with an exit-code test rather than eyeballing grep output, as the P6 ac-quality advisory asked.

E. stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL was dropped from the helper contract. No launch site sets stdin today, so mandating it would change child behaviour at all fourteen sites for no recorded reason.

Site line numbers were re-verified against origin/main and updated where they had drifted (authorship :43->:41, ci-snapshot :61->:62, engine-dir :188->:187, environ-assert :141->:140, external-isolation :63->:62, fixture-env :54->:67, git-floor :165->:164, live-Jira :162->:161, repo-isolation-guard :82->:81).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implementation landed for review as Gerrit change 2080 (Change-Id I15500125c881518b4686a4efddd5169865c361bd), commit db733093bb4.

Shape: tests/_nested_pytest.py exports run_nested_pytest(tmp_path, *args, env, timeout=None, cwd=REPO_ROOT, no_cacheprovider=True) plus BASETEMP_FLAG / NESTED_BASETEMP_NAME / nested_basetemp(tmp_path). All 14 launch sites converted; 109 insertions against 256 deletions across those 14 modules.

One defect the plan did not anticipate, found by running the work rather than reasoning about it: pytest's --basetemp does NOT create missing parent directories, it fails every child test with FileNotFoundError. tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py runs two nested invocations in one test, so each needs its own subdirectory of tmp_path, and neither existed. The helper now does Path(tmp_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) before launching, which is precisely the class of per-site re-decision this consolidation exists to remove. Covered by test_a_tmp_path_that_does_not_exist_yet_still_gets_a_usable_basetemp.

Mutation evidence, each perturbation applied to the live implementation and reverted; each killed a specific named test:
- drop the --basetemp append -> test_the_child_basetemp_is_owned_by_the_caller FAILED (assert False)
- env={**os.environ, **env} instead of verbatim -> test_the_caller_environment_is_forwarded_verbatim FAILED (the parent-only key leaked into the child)
- catch subprocess.TimeoutExpired and return a CompletedProcess -> test_a_timeout_propagates_to_the_caller FAILED (DID NOT RAISE TimeoutExpired)
- force no_cacheprovider on unconditionally -> test_the_cache_provider_suppression_is_optional FAILED
- re-wrap the CompletedProcess before returning -> test_the_call_contract_reaches_subprocess_run FAILED (result is not the same object)
- drop the mkdir -> test_a_tmp_path_that_does_not_exist_yet_still_gets_a_usable_basetemp FAILED

Guard evidence:
- reintroducing a hand-built launch in tests/_store_isolation.py -> test_the_launch_appears_only_in_the_helper FAILED and named the file and line
- the same launch annotated '# nested-pytest-ok: demo reason' -> GREEN, so the escape marker works
- renaming the helper definition -> test_the_helper_is_defined_exactly_once FAILED
- the guard first ran RED against all 14 real sites before any conversion, and is GREEN now

Acceptance-criteria commands run on the worktree: 'grep -rl ^def run_nested_pytest tests/ | wc -l' = 1; 'grep -rl "parent / .pytest." tests/ | wc -l' = 2; 'grep -rl -- --basetemp tests/ | wc -l' = 2 (tests/_nested_pytest.py and the unconverted tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py), down from 12. make lint and make typecheck both exit zero; the complexity ratchet reports new=0 increased=0.

All four pinning consumers pass unedited, as do the 14 converted modules and the two bare-console-script modules.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Fourteen test modules hand-build a nested pytest invocation (an argv list holding `sys.executable`,
`"-m"`, `"pytest"`), each re-deciding basetemp, timeout, cache plugin and env. The `--basetemp`
defect arrived as three separate CLOSED bugs (RCA: session log `0bd6-4729-e79e-433b`); all are
fixed, the duplication that made them three instalments is not. Three sites still lack
`--basetemp`: test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py:25, which EXECUTES three real
integration nodes and is a live instance of the defect (missed earlier for being
`pytest.mark.integration`), and the `--collect-only` children test_git_version_floor.py:164,
test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py:161.

## Approach
Add tests/_nested_pytest.py, imported as `from _nested_pytest import run_nested_pytest`:

    run_nested_pytest(tmp_path, *args, env, timeout=None, cwd=REPO_ROOT, no_cacheprovider=True)
        -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]

It builds `[sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", *args, "--basetemp", str(tmp_path / "nested-pytest")]`,
prepends `-p no:cacheprovider` when `no_cacheprovider`, and calls `subprocess.run` with
`capture_output=True, text=True`, cwd/env/timeout as keywords, and no `check`.

### Constraints the implementation MUST respect
- `env` is REQUIRED and forwarded VERBATIM — never merged onto `os.environ`, never re-wrapped, no
  key added or removed. Four sites hand the child a deliberately minimal two/three-key mapping so
  pytest's bounded mapping repr cannot truncate the sentinel away; widening it leaves those oracles
  green and vacuous: test_autodeploy_env_repr_security.py:31,
  test_environ_assert_repr_security.py:134, test_fixture_env_repr_security.py:49,
  test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py:189.
- Two sites pass NO `env` today and inherit `os.environ`; since `env` is required they convert with
  `env=subprocess_env()` (copies `os.environ` into the repr-safe mapping), NOT a minimal one:
  test_ci_workflow_parity.py:839 (`_collect_node_ids`) and test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:62.
  For the collector this is load-bearing — test_ci_workflow_parity_basetemp.py:32 sets
  `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT` via `monkeypatch.setenv` on the PARENT and asserts at :37-40 that the
  child honoured it; a minimal env drops it and the child then deletes another run's temp root.
- `_collect_node_ids(paths, selection)` keeps its two-argument signature (:9,33 of that module
  import and call it by name) and has no `tmp_path` fixture in scope, so it keeps its
  `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rebar-pytest-collect-")` and passes `Path(temp_dir)` as the
  helper's `tmp_path`. It also passes `no_cacheprovider=False`, matching the flag it omits today.
- test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:62 passes NO `cwd` today; it converts with `cwd=None` so the
  child still inherits the parent's working directory.
- Contract pinned by test_repo_isolation_deadline_heldout.py: `env` must survive as a plain `dict`
  (:39 supplies `{"PATH": "test-path"}`, so the helper may NOT call `SubprocessEnv` methods on it);
  `timeout` reaches `subprocess.run` as a KEYWORD (:42, asserted `>= 30`); the `CompletedProcess`
  is returned UNMODIFIED (:51, `result is nested_result`). `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` propagates,
  so test_repo_isolation_guard.py:100-104 keeps its own diagnostic conversion.
- These divergences stay at the call site as `*args` — do NOT normalise: `-n 0`, `-p no:randomly`,
  `-p conftest`, `-rs`, `--collect-only`, `--tb=<style>`, `--showlocals`, and the per-site timeouts
  30/90/300/None.
- Two sites are OUT of scope: test_scripts_import_convention.py:154 (bug 291e) and
  test_tests_import_convention.py:92 (bug a371) spawn the BARE `pytest` console script from a cwd
  outside the repo precisely so the repo root cannot reach `sys.path`. Converting them inserts cwd
  and destroys both reproductions.

## Guard construction
Follow the guard-test construction rule in parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`, adapted from
src/rebar to tests/ because the owner is a test helper. The construct has no distinctive single atom
surviving formatting — Black splits argv one element per line, so a source grep for `"-m", "pytest"`
returns ZERO hits on unmodified `main`, passing vacuously before and after this work. Branch 4 of
the rule therefore applies, in two parts:
1. an AST scan over tests/**/*.py for ANY list-or-tuple literal whose elements hold
   `sys.executable`, `"-m"`, `"pytest"` in consecutive positions. It must NOT be restricted to a
   literal in `subprocess.run`'s first argument: test_fixture_env_repr_security.py:54 binds the argv
   list to a local `command` first, so a call-argument-only scan finds 13 sites, not 14;
2. the definition count: exactly one `def run_nested_pytest` under tests/.

Owner module tests/_nested_pytest.py is exempt; escape marker `# nested-pytest-ok: <reason>`, reason
mandatory. The unquoted `-m pytest` (23 prose hits) is deliberately unmatched.

## Scope
New: tests/_nested_pytest.py, tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py,
tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py. Converted: exactly the 14 sites the
Guard-construction AST scan finds on `main` — one in tests/_store_isolation.py, one in
tests/integration/, one in tests/scripts/, eleven in tests/unit/. The three named in Context also
gain `--basetemp`.

Pinning consumers, unedited but run to prove the conversion, under tests/unit/:
test_repo_isolation_deadline_heldout.py, test_ci_workflow_parity_basetemp.py,
test_test_suite_store_isolation{,_heldout}.py. The `pytester.runpytest*` calls in
test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py and test_repo_isolation_guard.py stay unconverted — pytest already
owns their basetemp.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exactly one nested-pytest launch site under tests/ — the helper. Checked by
  `test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py::test_the_launch_appears_only_in_the_helper` (AST scan; a
  source grep would pass vacuously).
- [ ] Exactly one helper definition. Checked by
  `[ "$(grep -rl '^def run_nested_pytest' tests/ | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 1 ]`.
- [ ] Every nested run's basetemp is under the caller's `tmp_path`. Checked by
  `test_nested_pytest_helper.py::test_the_child_basetemp_is_owned_by_the_caller`.
- [ ] `--basetemp` is spelled in exactly two modules afterwards (twelve today) — the helper and the
  unconverted test_scripts_import_convention.py (so both console-script sites survive). Checked by `[ "$(grep -rl -- '--basetemp' tests/ | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 2 ]`.
- [ ] A caller-supplied env mapping reaches the child byte-identically, no key added or removed.
  Checked by `test_nested_pytest_helper.py::test_the_caller_environment_is_forwarded_verbatim`.
- [ ] `timeout` reaches `subprocess.run` as a keyword and the `CompletedProcess` is returned
  unmodified. Checked by test_repo_isolation_deadline_heldout.py passing unedited.
- [ ] `TimeoutExpired` propagates out of the helper (the hang case asserts the raise only, marked
  `# timing: hang-guard`). Checked by
  `test_nested_pytest_helper.py::test_a_timeout_propagates_to_the_caller`.
- [ ] Every per-site divergence above is preserved. Checked by the fourteen converted modules and
  four pinning consumers passing with no assertion edit.
- [ ] `make lint` exits zero.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits zero.
- [ ] `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT` still reaches the parity-collection child, which stays importable by
  name. Checked by test_ci_workflow_parity_basetemp.py unchanged.
- [ ] `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT` still reaches the store-isolation child. Checked by
  `test_test_suite_store_isolation.py::test_nested_pytest_does_not_clean_shared_numbered_temp_root`
  (all parametrisations) passing unchanged.
- [ ] The converted files pass the default `Verified` tier, the `--dist loadgroup` lane and the
  `integration` tier (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:657,672). Checked by CI.
